rule: When a deep carry-chain path (≥12 levels, CARRY4 cells ≥6) implements a multi-operand addition (≥3 addends) in a single carry-ripple tree, replace with a carry-save adder (CSA) tree that reduces to two operands before the final carry-propagate add, keeping all register boundaries identical.
applies_when: Path contains CARRY4 ≥6 AND logic depth ≥12 AND the timed addition combines ≥3 distinct 32-bit operands (here: h_reg + sum1 + ch + w_data + k_data = 5 operands feeding t1, then t1+t2 = 2-operand final add for a_new) AND route% < 70% (logic-bound, so logic restructuring helps) AND no pipeline register may be inserted
expected_effect: CSA tree collapses five-operand t1 sum and subsequent t1+t2 into two carry-propagate stages of roughly half the carry-chain depth, reducing the critical path from ~16 logic levels to ~8-10 levels with no latency change

evidence.declined_by_menu: The binding path is a 16-level carry-chain arithmetic path through the SHA-256 round function (t1+t2 → a_reg), and none of the menu strategies have their preconditions met: route% is below 70% (no max_fanout_16), no flag/decode comparison (no flag_precompute), no sign-extract idiom (no sign_select), 32-bit domain (no constant_lut), and no variable shifter (no shifter_mux_reduce).

note: Chip closure 11.98 -> 10.48 ns, 83.5 -> 95.4 MHz (+14.3%). Gate PASS (signature bit-identical to golden). Binding path moved HASH_BM -> HASH_SM, the second cone on the 2026-08-25 board, which is the mechanism. Artix-7 xc7a200tfbg676-1, OOC, ExtraTimingOpt/Explore/Explore. Prediction that CSA would lose to dedicated CARRY4 on FPGA was WRONG.

rule: When a_new = t1 + t2 and e_new = d_reg + t1 share the t1 addend, and t1 itself sums 5+ operands (h_reg, sum1, ch, k_data, w_data), replace the two-level ripple addition with a carry-save adder tree that reduces all addends to two before the final carry-propagate add, keeping all operations within the same combinational stage.
applies_when: Path contains CARRY4 chain depth >= 16 levels; the destination register is fed by a sum of 5 or more independent operands resolvable in the same clock cycle; no operand depends on the carry-out of another adder in the cone; tool has not already inferred CSA (confirmed by presence of deep carry chain in timing report).
expected_effect: Carry-propagate chain depth reduced from 5-operand ripple (~17 CARRY4) to 2-operand final add (~4 CARRY4 after CSA tree), cutting logic-stage count and slack deficit on this path.

evidence.declined_by_menu: The binding path is a deep carry-chain through a multi-operand adder (t1+t2 with 5+ addends), but none of the validated strategy menu entries apply: route% is below the max_fanout_16 threshold, there is no CE-flag precompute opportunity, no small-domain LUT, no sign-extract idiom, and no variable shifter; the only matching hypothesis (CSA reduction) is unvalidated.

note: Proposed on sha512_core at 192f during the run whose menu verdict was no_action. That verdict was itself caused by carry_chain_csa_reduction being rendered as unvalidated after its resolution record replaced its rule text (F48). Once the status rendering was fixed, the validated rule applied to the same cone and the applied edit reduced the five-operand t1 sum only. The shared-t1 variant across a_new and e_new was never applied and has no measurement. Superseded by carry_chain_csa_reduction, which covers the same cone with a simpler transformation and carries evidence at both 32-bit and 64-bit widths.
